keyQuestions.text: Which doc lines in README.md, AGENTS.md, CROSS-CLI.md and the runtime sync docs state an agent count, roster, or agent file location that disagrees with `.skilled/agents/*.md` and `agent-registry.json`?
Which doc lines misdescribe an individual agent's role, tool allowlist, or permission block relative to that agent's `.skilled/agents/<name>.md` frontmatter?
Which doc lines state agent status values, routing rules, or model pins that contradict the agent frontmatter, the registry, or the runtime generator?

Which skill, command, feature-catalog and manual-testing-playbook docs describe agent sync mechanisms or runtime copy locations that no longer match the generator and the checked-in runtime agent folders?
Which runtime agent copies (.claude, .codex, .cursor, .devin, .dsh, .opencode, .pi, .vibe) diverge from their `.skilled/agents/*.md` source in a way a doc claims is synchronized?

keyFindings.text: `.skilled/agents/README.txt:8` states "Sibling runtime: .claude/agents/ (.md)" — one sibling. Seven runtime copies exist (`.claude`, `.codex`, `.cursor`, `.devin`, `.dsh`, `.pi`, `.vibe`), and the same file's next paragraph already refers to "the `.codex` and `.pi` trees", so the sibling line contradicts its own file. [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/README.txt:8] [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/README.txt:5]

`.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:121` states "`.skilled` declares `mode: subagent` for ten agents, `mode: all` for `markdown` and `mode: primary` for `orchestrate`." The actual split is nine / one / one: `mode: subagent` is declared by `ai-council`, `code`, `context`, `debug`, `deep-research`, `deep-review`, `design`, `prompt-improver` and `review`; `markdown` is `mode: all`; `orchestrate` is `mode: primary`. The sentence overcounts subagents by one and its three-way split sums to twelve against an eleven-agent roster. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:121] [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/markdown.md:5] [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/orchestrate.md:5]

`.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:16` states "Six runtime trees ship the same eleven agents: `.skilled/agents/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.cursor/agents/`, `.pi/agents/`, `.codex/agents/` and `.devin/agents/`." Two further trees ship all eleven and are omitted: `.dsh/agents/` (11 `.patch.yml`) and `.vibe/agents/` (11 `.toml`). The same file's frontmatter description repeats the "six runtime agent trees" count. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:16] [SOURCE: .skilled/CROSS-CLI.md:77] [SOURCE: .skilled/CROSS-CLI.md:78]

`.skilled/bin/check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs:6` states "Every agent is authored once under `.opencode/agents/<name>.md`". `.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:30` designates `.skilled/agents/` as the "authored source of truth", and `.opencode/agents` is a symlink to `../.skilled/agents`, so `.opencode/agents/<name>.md` is the same file as `.skilled/agents/<name>.md` rather than a separate authoring location. The checker's own `AGENTS_DIR` constant points at `.opencode/agents`, which resolves through the symlink, so the comment names a path that only exists because of the link it does not mention. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs:6] [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:30]

`.skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs:57`-`:68` enumerates the roster surfaces as `cursor`, `devin`, `opencode`, `codex` and `pi`. `.dsh/agents/` and `.vibe/agents/` are absent from both the `LINKED` and `AUTHORED` lists, so the check that `.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:58` advertises as failing "when a runtime is missing an agent" cannot see two of the eight runtime trees. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs:57] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs:65] [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:58]

`.skilled/CROSS-CLI.md:57` states "`.skilled/agents/` is canonical for the Claude fork, the Codex TOMLs and the Pi copies, while `.claude/agents/` is canonical for Cursor and Devin." The same file's generator table two sections later attributes `.dsh/agents/` to `sync-agents-dsh.cjs` and `.vibe/agents/` to `sync-agents-vibe.cjs`, both reading `.skilled/agents/`, so the "two upstreams" enumeration is missing two generated trees it documents itself. [SOURCE: .skilled/CROSS-CLI.md:57] [SOURCE: .skilled/CROSS-CLI.md:77] [SOURCE: .skilled/CROSS-CLI.md:78]

`.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/manual-testing-playbook/tooling-and-scripts/template-compliance-contract-enforcement-blocks-non-compliant.md:184` tells the operator to "Inspect ... `.skilled/agents/speckit.toml`". No `speckit` agent exists in the eleven-agent roster, and `.skilled/agents/` holds `.md` files, not `.toml`. The same file's evidence block at lines 64-68 already records `MISSING .skilled/agents/speckit.md` and `MISSING .skilled/agents/speckit.toml`, so the follow-up line points at a path the file itself proves absent. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/manual-testing-playbook/tooling-and-scripts/template-compliance-contract-enforcement-blocks-non-compliant.md:184] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/manual-testing-playbook/tooling-and-scripts/template-compliance-contract-enforcement-blocks-non-compliant.md:65]

`README.md:963` states the eleven agents are "mirrored for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin and Pi (`.<runtime>/agents/`)". `.dsh/agents/` and `.vibe/agents/` are omitted, so the README names five of the seven runtime copies. `AGENTS.md:282` names all eight agent directories, including `.dsh/agents/` and `.vibe/agents/`, so the two root docs disagree with each other as well as with the tree. [SOURCE: README.md:963] [SOURCE: AGENTS.md:282]

`.skilled/agents/README.txt:9` states "Inventory rule: if an agent file is not present in this directory, it is not a live runtime surface here." `.claude/agents/Explore.md` is a live runtime surface in the sibling tree the next line names, and is not present in `.skilled/agents/`. The rule is defensible only if "here" is read as strictly `.skilled/agents/` (and, through the symlink, `.opencode/agents/`); read as an inventory rule for the roster it is falsified by the file the same README's model paragraph goes on to name. [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/README.txt:9] [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/README.txt:8] [SOURCE: .claude/agents/Explore.md:1]

`.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/SKILL.md:264` gives the iteration status enum as `complete | timeout | error | stuck | insight` — five values. `.skilled/agents/deep-review.md:236` allows six, `complete | timeout | error | stuck | insight | thought`, and the deep-research sibling at `.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/SKILL.md:225` lists all six. The deep-review skill doc therefore omits `thought`, the analytical-only status, and its explanatory list at `:266` explains only `insight`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/SKILL.md:264] [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/deep-review.md:236] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/SKILL.md:225]

`.vibe/SYNC.md:37` states "One `.toml` per `.skilled/agents/*.md`, `README.md` excepted, named by the source stem." The exception file is `.skilled/agents/README.txt`, not `README.md`; there is no `README.md` in `.skilled/agents/`. The same wrong filename appears in the generated-block comment convention the roster writer emits. [SOURCE: .vibe/SYNC.md:37] [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/README.txt:1]

`.vibe/SYNC.md:39` labels its second column "`mode` (dropped)" and `.vibe/SYNC.md:53` states "the OpenCode `permission` map and the `mode` value do not travel into Vibe." Both contradict `.vibe/SYNC.md:37` in the same section, which says the render "adds `agent_type = \"subagent\"` when the source declares `mode: subagent`", and contradict the generated tree: nine of the eleven `.vibe/agents/*.toml` files carry `agent_type = "subagent"`. `mode` does travel, as `agent_type`; only the `all` and `primary` values are dropped. [SOURCE: .vibe/SYNC.md:39] [SOURCE: .vibe/SYNC.md:53] [SOURCE: .vibe/SYNC.md:37] [SOURCE: .vibe/agents/context.toml:3]

`README.md:1017` describes Deep Review as "audits one review pass, read-only on code". `.skilled/agents/deep-review.md:7`-`:9` grants `write: allow`, `edit: allow` and `bash: allow`, so the agent is not read-only by tool surface; only its behavioral rule forbids code changes (`.skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/SKILL.md:260`, "The review loop is observation-only. No code changes during audit."). The contrast is sharpest against `review`, which genuinely is read-only (`write: deny`, `edit: deny`) and which `README.md:983` describes as "never edits". [SOURCE: README.md:1017] [SOURCE: .skilled/agents/deep-review.md:7] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/SKILL.md:260] [SOURCE: README.md:983]

ruledOutDirections.text: **`.claude/agents/Explore.md` as an orphaned mirror.** It is documented as deliberate in three places: `.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:2.5` ("`Explore.md` is not a roster agent"), `.skilled/CROSS-CLI.md:55` ("a Claude-only agent with no counterpart in `.skilled/agents/`"), and `.skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs:52` (`CLAUDE_ONLY_AGENTS = new Set(['Explore'])`). Not drift.

**`.claude` model pins** (same section). Verified: `context.md`, `markdown.md` and `Explore.md` declare `model: haiku`; `prompt-improver.md` declares `model: sonnet`; no other `.claude` agent declares a model. The claim holds.

**`.codex` model pin** (`.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:2.5`). Verified: all eleven `.codex/agents/*.toml` carry `model = "gpt-6-luna"`, with `model_reasoning_effort = "high"` except `context` (`low`) and `markdown` (`medium`). The claim holds exactly.

**`.opencode/agents/` as a non-symlinked copy.** `ls -la .opencode` shows `agents -> ../.skilled/agents`, so `CROSS-CLI.md:36` ("Symlinked ... `agents`") and `README.md:963` ("links to the same `.skilled/agents/` source") are both correct. The apparent "real files" in a directory listing are the symlink target's files.
**`.pi` model absence** (same section). Verified: no `model:` key in any `.pi/agents/*.md`. The claim holds.
**`.skilled/agents/README.txt:4` "agent definitions for the OpenCode runtime".** Literally true because `.opencode/agents` is a symlink to this directory. Not reported as drift.

**`.skilled` as "the only tree that carries a permission map"** (`.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:68`). `.opencode/agents` resolves to `.skilled/agents`, so no second distinct tree carries a permission map. The claim holds.
**`Agent`/`task` grant** (`.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:2.4`). Verified: only `ai-council` and `orchestrate` carry `task: allow`; the other nine carry `task: deny`. The claim holds.
**`temperature` split** (`.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:2.2`). Verified: `0.2` for `debug` and `design`, `0.1` for the other nine. The claim holds.

Grepping for a numeric agent count (`eleven agents`, `11 agents`) across the repo returns almost nothing outside the crosswalk and `README.md:963`; the roster is described by enumeration rather than by count, so count-based greps are a weak detector for this topic.

The feature catalogs contain no agent-roster claims. The only hits are handler-table rows naming `.skilled/agents/review.md`, `.skilled/agents/orchestrate.md` and `.skilled/agents/debug.md`, all of which exist and match their described roles.

**`ai-council` as a LEAF that grants `task: allow`.** Not a contradiction: `.skilled/agents/ai-council.md:44` states "The AI Council is a LEAF by default. It dispatches council seats only when the prompt states that the operator invoked it directly", and `.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:2.4` documents `Agent`/`task` as the nested-delegation grant. The registry's `tier: LEAF` and the frontmatter agree on the default.
**`ai-council`'s `max_rounds` default of 3 (`agent-registry.json:47`).** `.skilled/agents/ai-council.md:389` states "up to `max_rounds` (default 3)". The claim holds.
**`code`'s "seven dispatch modes" (`README.md:975`).** `.skilled/agents/code.md:261` states "Mode: <one of the 7 dispatch modes>". The count matches.

**`markdown` as `mode: all` while the registry calls it LEAF.** The crosswalk (`.skilled/bin/agent-mirror-crosswalk.md:121`) and `.vibe/SYNC.md:48` both report `mode: all` correctly. The tension is inside the agent file itself (`.skilled/agents/markdown.md:4` `mode: all` against `:24` "Dedicated LEAF executor"), not between a doc and the agent. Out of scope for a docs-drift finding; recorded for the next focus.

**`never auto-dispatched` for `@debug`.** Consistent across `agent-registry.json:123`, `.skilled/agents/debug.md:26`, `.skilled/agents/README.txt:24` and `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/debugging/universal-debugging-methodology.md:29`. The registry's `dispatchers: ["operator"]` matches. No drift.
**`Only @orchestrate dispatches it` (`README.md:977`) for `@code`.** `agent-registry.json` gives `code` exactly one dispatcher, `orchestrate`. The claim holds.

**`orchestrate.md`'s generated roster blocks as drift.** The routing table at `.skilled/agents/orchestrate.md:77`-`:88`, the tier table at `:98` and the agent-files block at `:171` are all generated from `agent-registry.json` and match it row for row: eleven rows, priorities 1-11, every tier `LEAF` except the orchestrator itself. No drift.

**`sync-agent-roster.cjs` as a broken reference.** The script exists at `.skilled/bin/sync-agent-roster.cjs` and is documented at `.skilled/bin/README.md:180`. The generated-block comments that name it are accurate.

Grepping for a status enum by its literal pipe-separated form finds only five files, and four of them agree. The vocabulary is restated in prose in most places, so a grep for `status` alone returns hundreds of unrelated hits. The enum is a narrow, high-yield target; the surrounding prose is not.

The README's per-agent role paragraphs are accurate for nine of the eleven agents. Only the Deep Review paragraph makes a tool-surface claim that the frontmatter contradicts, so this angle is close to exhausted after one pass.
